commits.summary: Brief for a feature loop that makes build.py a runner of claims, attempts and evidence
commits.body:
Adds llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration-review.md, an outside review of examples/tools/build.py at 4c279ba6 kept verbatim as the loop's fixed input. It finds that a crashed verifier counts as a counterexample, D1 can check an old contract against new bytecode, missing TLC coverage reads as none, and several properties collapse into one statement. It proposes a claim/attempt/conclusion/evidence format and four developer features: check this bug fix, JVM replay with a JUnit test, external artifacts as inputs, and proof experiments.

Adds llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md, the brief feature-loop.sh runs. It cuts the review's five phases into 14 steps of about one cycle (1a-5b), each with an acceptance criterion. It sets the working rules (runner tests with mocked subprocesses in a new examples/tools/test_build.py, proofs queued through the pipeline, recorded results never edited by hand, nothing weakened), four open questions for the user with the default the loop takes, Progress, Loop settings (new session f1a97af5, claude-opus-5-5, high effort) and Loop until.

commits.summary: build-orchestration brief: Phase 4's developer features deferred
commits.body:
By the user's decision, the review's developer-facing features (check this bug fix, JVM replay with a JUnit test, external artifacts as inputs) move out of the plan into a Deferred section kept for context. They would add considerations that are useful to developers but not novel, and make the proof experiments harder to run; they will be revisited separately. The brief now states its focus: data structures, interfaces and evaluations for proof work, built so that such features can later be added as renderings of evidence already held. Step 3b gains typed witness values, target descriptors, argument mappings and artifact identities for that reason. Phase 5 follows Phase 3. The two open questions that belonged to Phase 4 moved with it, and the Done-when table drops its row.

Verified by reading the brief's headings and cross-references after the move; no code changed.

commits.summary: build.py: how a verifier's run ended is decided before its verdict (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 1a of the build-orchestration brief. Before, build.py classified a jvmcontract or Java-verifier run as verified on exit 0, unverifiable when the output said 'cannot be verified', and violation otherwise. A verifier killed by signal 9 with empty output was recorded as 'Violation: counterexample found', with no counterexample, and matched an example that expected a violation. write_evidence() also wrote an empty SARIF report when the verifier wrote none. The review's findings were checked against the code at c4fa2f64 and all still held.

Now execution_status() and conclude() (and tlc_conclusion() for TLC, run directly for Box Office or through jvmcontract tlc --json) first record result.execution: completed, timed-out, killed (a negative code or 128+N), invalid-output (nothing printed, malformed JSON, exit 1 with no evidence or no report) or tool-error (any other exit code; a TLC run that ended without a verdict). Only a completed run has a verdict. A violation needs the evidence the runner read (counterexamples, changed cases, capability or boundary changes, new ! lines, a trace) and the verifier's SARIF report. A run without a verdict records verdict null, the label '⚠ No verdict: <reason>' and expectation not-evaluable, and matchesExpected is false. build.py exits 1 and prints a line the pipeline's example:unexpected signal matches. The runs that give the verdict are recorded, not fatal, on exit code 2. Setup steps (update, tla, compile) still stop the runner, now also on a signal. A missing report is not made up, and a stale result.sarif or statement.java from an earlier run is removed, so a folder never shows another run's evidence. Each D1 configuration also records its status. The page of a run without a verdict says so in place of the findings.

Choices: a run that did not complete gets verdict null, not 'unverifiable'. That is the option that reports less, and otherwise a crash would match example 003, which expects unverifiable. 'Why the verdict is right' still prints the authored explanation; separating it from the observed evidence is step 3c. The per-configuration termination reason beyond the status is step 2b.

Verified: the new examples/tools/test_build.py (25 unittest cases, mocked processes) covers signal 9 with empty output, 137 and 134, exit codes 2/3/101, timeouts, empty output, exit 1 without evidence or report, malformed TLC JSON, TLC killed or late inside the tool, a violation without a trace, rendering and schema validation of a no-verdict result, and main()'s exit code and pipeline signal. Recomputing every recorded result's expectation under the new rule gives exactly what was recorded, and every recorded violation has its evidence. All 140 committed results validate against the extended schema, which accepts the old shape. verification/test_pipeline.py passes. build.py --render-only renders every page. Eight pages changed only because they had drifted from their committed results (timings, and a renderer sentence on 110); nothing in them comes from this change.

Verification jobs, one per approach, check that the verdicts are unchanged and that result.json gains execution: 20261105-112331-example-126-b9-under-build-py-s-executio (B9 JBMC), 20261105-112331-example-132-b9-under-build-py-s-executio (B9 native), 20261105-112331-example-017-b11-under-build-py-s-executi (B11), 20261105-112331-example-110-b12-under-build-py-s-executi (B12), 20261105-112331-example-101-d1-under-build-py-s-executio (D1), 20261105-112331-example-003-b8-under-build-py-s-executio (B8 Box Office, expected unverifiable).

commits.summary: build.py: a requested example that doesn't run never exits 0 (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 1b of the build-orchestration brief. Before this change, build.py silently did nothing for an unknown id or a real-world one and still exited 0. An app it didn't know, or an approach with no runner, made it sys.exit in load_example, which also broke rendering the router. Now an argument that is not the three-digit id of an example folder exits 2 before anything runs. That includes a folder name, an unknown flag, and --index-only with ids.

A requested example that build.py can't run prints 'NNN-name: not-executed (why)' and fails the run with exit 1. That covers a real-world example (105-109), a subject file under no app, an approach the app has no runner for, and a D1 symbol no TLA+ model is built around. not_executable() gives the reason. app_of() returns None, and find_model() is model_of() without the exit. Running every example still means every constructed one, so the real-world ones are left out without failing. --render-only with an explicit id it can't render exits 1.

Choice taken: nothing is written for an example that was not executed. An earlier result.json is evidence of its own run and stays. A result that no longer matches its inputs is step 3c's to show as stale, and I didn't overwrite evidence with a non-attempt. The pipeline gains an example:not-executed signal. submit --example now refuses a real-world id with a message, where it used to fail with a KeyError on expected. Every queued job runs build.py on one constructed id, so none of them changes. The pipeline README's sample submit used example 105, a real-world id since; it now uses the next free number, 146.

Verified: examples/tools/test_build.py, 33 tests, 8 of them new (unknown id, a non-id argument, a real-world id alone and next to a constructed one, every example, an app nobody builds with its result.json left alone, the reasons, render-only); verification/test_pipeline.py, 16 tests, 1 new. By hand: 'build.py 999' and '108 017x' exit 2, and 'build.py 108' prints the not-executed line and exits 1. A full --render-only exits 0 and leaves every page and the router unchanged. No recorded result moved.

Verification pending: job 20261105-113118-example-025-b8-under-build-py-s-strict-s (verification/jobs/) checks that an ordinary run of one constructed example still prints 'as expected' and exits 0. The six step-1a jobs (20261105-112331-*) had not run when this cycle started.

commits.summary: build.py: regression proofs read from equivalence --json, and the page says where a witness was replayed (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 1c of the build-orchestration brief. run_tool_equivalence() now runs jvmcontract equivalence with --json and reads the library's Outcome instead of parsing its console text. That covers the verdict, the witness, the domain, the proof line, the problem, the vacuity and the statement's path. The console text in the outcome is still written as verifier-output.txt. A new conclude_outcome() requires the exit code to agree with the outcome's verdict, and output that is not an outcome, the plain text included, is invalid-output rather than a verdict. A violation still needs its witness and the SARIF report.

The library's equivalence Outcome gains search and replay. search is the checker run the verdict comes from: the engine (jbmc or native), the checker, the seconds, the unwinding and array bounds, the input range, the reason the own checker gave no verdict under --engine auto, and the own checker's numbers. Those are bmc::Stats, carried on JbmcResult.native. replay records that the witness was run on both versions in jvmcontract's bytecode interpreter, and whether it reproduced. Results record both as search (with sharedCallees) and replay, and a violation's counterexample gains found (the input before shrinking) and shrinkRuns. The schema, examples/README.md, examples/approaches.md and lib/README.md describe them.

The page's replay sentence used to say 'on the JVM' for every B9 example. It now comes from replay, or for results recorded before it, from the proof line. A full --render-only exits 0. On 17 pages the sentence now reads 'in jvmcontract's bytecode interpreter', and the 2 Box Office pages, whose Java verifier does replay on the JVM (and records replay.by jvm), still say 'on the JVM'. Nothing else on any page moved, and no recorded result.json changed. B11 (prove) still parses text through symbolic_fields(), which is step 1d.

Verified with examples/tools/test_build.py (46 tests, 13 new): JSON fixtures for a violation, a verified run and a vacuous one, an exit code that disagrees with the verdict, text where JSON was asked for, a witness that does not reproduce, the own checker's numbers, the patched copy's root removed from the outcome, the wording for every recorded B9 violation, and schema validation. Also cargo test --release in lib/ (two integration tests now check search and replay), and verification/test_pipeline.py (16 tests).

Jobs: 20261105-114501-example-128-b9-jbmc-read-from-equivalenc (a JBMC violation), 20261105-114501-example-120-b9-jbmc-shared-callees-read (JBMC with shared callees), 20261105-114501-example-143-b9-own-checker-read-from-equ (a native violation), 20261105-114502-example-144-b9-own-checker-vacuous-read (vacuous), and 20261105-114502-example-006-b9-box-office-java-verifier (Box Office). The seven jobs from 1a and 1b had not run at the start of this cycle.

Corrections to the brief: the review's 'replayed it on the JVM' was right for the Box Office examples, whose Java verifier really replays on the JVM, and wrong only for jvmcontract's apps. The brief's 'summary line's numbers' are taken here as the proof line's numbers plus the own checker's statistics, which until now were only in bmc.log.

commits.summary: build.py: every property of a target keeps its own result, read from prove --json (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 1d of the build-orchestration brief. run_tool_property() used to parse jvmcontract prove's console text with regexes, which picked one assertion, one witness and one proof line out of however many properties a method had, and looked for a single harness where the tool writes one per property (property-N). Example 071, whose VoteRule#grant has three properties, recorded statement: null as a result. It now runs prove --json and keeps every property in a new result field, properties: its assumption, assertion, throws clauses as checked, verdict, domain, proof line, problem, vacuity, witness (with found and shrinkRuns), search and replay. With several properties, each entry also has its work directory and its harness, copied as statement-N.java.

The verdict is computed over the properties by property_headline(), every one of them required: a violation when any is refuted, verified only when all hold, unverifiable otherwise, with unresolved properties kept visible beside a refuted one. A violation needs every refuted property's witness and the SARIF report. The exit code must agree with the headline, and output that is not a list of outcomes (the plain text included) is invalid-output. A verified headline is vacuous when any of its properties is. A refuted one is not, but the property's own record keeps its vacuity. The label counts the properties ('counterexample found to 1 of 3 properties, 1 unresolved'). The flat property, domain, proof, problem and statement are the headline property's (the first refuted, else the first unresolved, else the first), so a single-property result has its old shape plus properties. The page gets a table of the properties, a witness for each refuted one (saying it was replayed in jvmcontract's bytecode interpreter), a proof line per property and a statement per property. Results recorded before this step have no properties and render as before: a full --render-only rewrote no page, and all 140 recorded results validate against the extended schema. symbolic_fields(), the last text parser of a proof, is gone.

In the library, property::Outcome gains search and replay, as equivalence's did in 1c, and throws_checked: the clauses with the exception named in full, which is the form the recorded results took from the text. replay.reproduced is false when the property calls the method under proof, since only the harness can evaluate that, so the violation rests on the checker's word. The choice is the conservative one: it claims no reproduction the interpreter did not show. lib/README.md documents prove --json, examples/README.md the result fields, and approaches.md the rule for several properties.

Verified: test_build.py has 59 tests (14 new in PropertyRunnerTest, whose shared setup moved to a RunnerCase base class with no tests of its own). They cover the 071 shape, every mix of headlines, a refuted property without its witness, an unknown verdict, an exit code that disagrees, vacuity over several properties, throws clauses, stale statements removed and a schema check. cargo test --release: 116 unit tests pass and 49 of 50 integration tests pass in the full parallel run. The one failure was the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs, whose own-checker regression proof of Pricing#total hit the solver's time limit, after the new property assertions in it had passed, in a run that took 630 s. Run again on its own with the other two touched tests, it passes (3 tests in 16 s). test_pipeline.py passes. No recorded result moved. Phase 1 of the brief is done, and 2a is next.

Jobs: 20261105-122210-example-071-b11-three-properties-read-fr (three outcomes, two verified and one refuted, with statement-3.java), 20261105-122210-example-053-b11-throws-clause-verified-r (one verified property with a throws clause, unchanged) and 20261105-122210-example-050-b11-arrays-shrunk-witness-re (one refuted property over arrays with a shrunk witness, unchanged). The twelve jobs from 1a to 1c had not run at the start of this cycle.

commits.summary: build.py: every D1 model checks the rule that was built, and a contract changed unasked is a violation (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 2a of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md, from section 1B of the outside review: a D1 model was generated from the committed contract unless behaviourChangeIntended was true, so a kernel a refactor changed was checked as it was before the patch. The gap still held at this commit. run_tool_tlc() regenerated contracts only for an intended change, and jvmcontract tla reads whatever contract file it is given. Box Office's run_tlc() had the same condition.

Now run_tool_tlc() derives the contract of every generated operator from the patched classes (jvmcontract derive) and generates the operator from that, and Box Office's run_tlc() runs :ticketing-domain:updateContracts on every run. The result records each operator in modelContracts: connection 'verified' when the derived contract is the committed one, 'derived' when it differs, with rowsChanged and allowed. behaviourChangeIntended decides only whether a difference is allowed. One that isn't is a violation whatever TLC found. Its diff goes in contractDiff and the SARIF report gets a contract-changed result, while TLC's own verdict and label stay in modelVerdict and modelSummary. A contract that can't be derived leaves the run without a verdict (tool-error), and TLC doesn't run. The page leads with an unapproved difference, or otherwise ends with where each rule comes from. The result schema, the example schema's behaviourChangeIntended, examples/README.md and approaches.md describe it.

Choices, taken as the conservative option: a difference that changes only an outcome's reason counts as a changed contract, though the model doesn't read reasons. A violation from an unapproved difference keeps the model's coverage and vacuity as TLC's run gave them. TLC's violation stays the headline when both fail. For a change not meant to alter behaviour, contractDiff holds only the operators' contracts, not the rest of the module's.

New example 146 is example 060's patch (a leader's election-timeout case folded into the others as dead code) declared as a refactor, behaviourChangeIntended false. The old runner checked the committed rule there; the new one finds the unapproved case and TLC's LeadersNeverCampaign trace on the rule as built.

Verified: test_build.py passes 69 tests, 10 of them new. They cover a kernel changed unasked (checked as built, then failed), an unchanged kernel, an intended change, a change to a reason alone, a contract that can't be derived, TLC's violation beside a changed contract, the page, the schema, and Box Office both ways. test_pipeline.py passes. --render-only over every example exits 0 and no page moved, because results recorded before this have no modelContracts. Deriving the operators inline for the non-intended examples 090, 091 and 094 gave the committed contracts byte for byte. For 146 it gave one RoleMachine case changed.

Jobs: 20261105-124133-example-146-d1-raft-election-a-kernel-ch, 20261105-124134-example-090-d1-2pc-trace-validation-with, 20261105-124134-example-104-d1-raft-replication-with-its, 20261105-124134-example-076-d1-circuit-breaker-with-its, 20261105-124134-example-012-d1-box-office-regenerates-th. The fifteen earlier jobs of this run had not run at the start of the cycle.

commits.summary: build.py: TLC coverage that was not read stays unknown, and each configuration's result is kept as it completes (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 2b of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md, from section 1D and 4 of the outside review. A verified D1 run whose coverage was missing used to count as one in which no step took any row, so a change could be labelled vacuous on no evidence. The gap was also in the library: jvmcontract tlc read an output with no coverage statistics, or an operator the statistics did not list, as zero counts for every row. OperatorCoverage now has 'listed', and the report says 'unknown' for an operator that is not listed. build.py's tlc_coverage() records coverage.status (complete, partial or unavailable) over the operators the verdict depends on. Each configuration records its verdict, status, reason, coverageStatus and listed operators, and each altered row records its operator and the configurations under which it was not counted (unknownUnder). Only complete coverage can make a verdict vacuous, and a jvmcontract without the flag gives unavailable. The page says 'no verdict: timed out' for an unfinished run that has no verdict, where it used to say 'stopped at the counterexample', and it says what is not known.

Each configuration's TLC result is now kept as soon as it completes (tlc_checkpointed_run), under the SHA-256 of everything the run depends on: every .tla and .cfg in the model's directory (the generated operators and recorded runs among them), the standard modules, the command, jvmcontract, TLC's jar and java -version. A result is reused only when both the fingerprint and the stored inputs match, and a run that did not complete is never kept. A configuration that can't be run (its trace writer fails, the tool can't start) becomes its own tool-error run, so the earlier configurations keep their results. The result's 'checkpoints' and the page say which results were reused. Results are kept in $BUILD_CHECKPOINTS, else in the git-ignored examples/.checkpoints, and BUILD_CHECKPOINTS=off keeps none. The pipeline points the variable at .state/checkpoints, so a job submitted again after a timeout reruns only what had not completed.

Choices made without the user, taking the conservative option: checkpoints are working state, not committed evidence (the durable evidence bundle is step 3b), and the heap TLC is given is not part of the fingerprint, since it decides whether a run completes, not what a completed run found. The brief names a single 'coverageStatus' on tlc_coverage(). The result has coverage.status overall and coverageStatus for each configuration, because one configuration's missing statistics should not hide what another's show. Box Office's own run_tlc() reads no coverage, and its coverage stays null as before.

Verified: test_build.py has 80 tests, 11 of them new. They cover missing coverage, an unlisted operator, complete coverage both ways, an old tool, a timed-out configuration beside a violated one, recorded results rendering as before, a later configuration's error keeping the earlier one and the rerun reusing it, a run without a verdict not kept, changed inputs or tools running again, a stored result whose inputs differ, and checkpoints off. test_pipeline.py has 17 tests (one new, for the variable), and cargo test passes (166). --render-only over every example exits 0 and no page moved. Examples/README.md, approaches.md, verification/README.md and the schema describe the new fields.

Jobs: 20261105-125705-example-072-d1-vacuous-coverage-status-c, 20261105-125706-example-074-d1-vacuous-role-machine-row, 20261105-125706-example-083-d1-changed-rows-taken-only-u, 20261105-125706-example-093-d1-2pc-participant-crashes-c, 20261105-125706-example-099-d1-raft-replication-liveness. No B9, B11 or B12 job, since nothing they run changed. The twenty jobs of steps 1a to 2a had not run at the start of this cycle.

commits.summary: build.py: one plan of each run, which the pipeline's job requirements come from (verification pending)
commits.body:
plan(example) in examples/tools/build.py resolves, from example.json alone and without side effects, what a run takes: app and module, the build adapter and what it copies, the runner, the claim (target, file, behaviourChangeIntended, and for B9 the intended inputs, previous symbol and arguments, result relation), the engine and the exact flags of the proof, the tools it calls (required, and optional: JBMC under engine auto), the D1 model with every configuration and generated operator, and the files it writes. run() executes the plan, the B9/B11 runners pass its flags (proof_options, replacing engine_flag), and build.py --plan [ID ...] prints plans as JSON. The scratch directory is made on first use, so importing build.py makes nothing.

verification/pipeline.py's example_job_parts() imports build.py and requires the plan's tools. The 15 native-engine examples no longer require JBMC, Box Office B12 jobs require jvmcontract (verifier built at the job's commit, build memory reserved), and a constructed example build.py does not run is refused with the reason. The job format is unchanged; queued jobs run as before. Choice: optional tools are required too, the conservative reading, since a job that may call JBMC must run where JBMC is.

Verified: test_build.py 90 tests (new: every recorded example planned with subprocess, copies, temp dirs and scratch refused; engines; Box Office B8/B9/B12; D1 model files exist; runner flags; --plan; pipeline requirements equal the plan's for every recorded example), test_pipeline.py 20 tests (new: native vs JBMC vs auto requirements, B12 requires jvmcontract and gets the build memory reservation, an unrunnable example is refused). --render-only over every example exits 0 and no page moved.

Jobs 20261105-130853-example-145-b9-own-checker-array-bound-1 (native, --max-array-length 12 from the plan) and 20261105-130853-example-113-b12-box-office-with-jvmcontr (B12 now requiring jvmcontract). The 25 earlier jobs had not run at the start of this cycle.

Brief: Progress records 3a; next is 3b. The rest of the brief still holds.

commits.summary: build.py: each run is an attempt at a frozen claim, and publishes one checked bundle of evidence (verification pending)
commits.body:
Step 3b of llm-dlc/loops/build-orchestration.md, first half. Under open question 1's default, result.json gains four blocks next to the flat fields, which are unchanged. claim is frozen before anything is built and written into the attempt's own directory as claim.json. It holds the plan's statement of what is checked, the scope (array bound, and for B9 the intended inputs), and SHA-256 fingerprints of the patch, of the copied sources before and after it (build output left out; build files, contracts and models in), and for D1 of each model file. Its id is their digest: another input or scope is another claim, and the engine is not part of it. attempt records the engine and flags, each tool's identity (Java, javac and JBMC versions, the Gradle distribution, the SHA-256 of jvmcontract and of TLC's jar), the bytecode built, the pipeline job (VERIFY_JOB_ID, VERIFY_SOURCE_COMMIT, VERIFY_WORKDIR), the time and the execution. For jvmcontract proofs it also records exploration: complete only for a verified proof, which checks unwinding assertions, and otherwise unknown. conclusion gives established, refuted or unresolved for the claim and for each obligation (a B11 target's properties, a D1 model's configurations, each generated operator's contract as built). bundle lists each evidence file with its SHA-256 and size.

Runners now write into the attempt's directory, never into the example's folder. check_result() validates the whole result against the schema and the bundle against the files before anything is published. publish() then renames each file in, removes evidence of an earlier run that the bundle does not list, and writes result.json last. bundle_problems() names any file that is not the run's: one changed, missing, or not listed. A missing jsonschema module now stops the run; it used to skip validation. The schema, examples/README.md and build.py's docstring describe the format.

Verified: test_build.py has 102 tests (12 new, including run() itself on 126's real patch and Crosscut's sources with the runner mocked, main() refusing to publish a mismatched bundle, and a claim id that moves with the bound but not the engine), and test_pipeline.py's 20 pass. A real run of 025 (B8) in a temporary copy of examples/ gave the four blocks, flat fields identical to the committed result, and a folder matching its bundle. No page moved under --render-only, and no committed result was rewritten. The twenty-seven earlier jobs had not run at the start of this cycle.

Jobs 20261105-131902-example-014-b8-quorum-recorded-as-a-clai, 20261105-131902-example-062-d1-raft-election-several-con, 20261105-131902-example-071-b11-three-properties-recorde, 20261105-131902-example-111-b12-box-office-recorded-as-a, 20261105-131902-example-129-b9-jbmc-verified-recorded-as and 20261105-131902-example-133-b9-own-checker-verified-reco: one per approach.

Where the brief differs from what was built: it lists before/after bytecode and the pipeline's VERIFY_* among the claim's fingerprints. The bytecode is built after the claim is frozen, and a job id differs on every run, so the claim fingerprints the sources the bytecode is compiled from, and the attempt records the bytecode and the job. A different compiler on the same sources is therefore another attempt at the same claim. Publishing is not one atomic step: the files are renamed one by one and result.json goes last, so an interrupted publish leaves files that don't match their bundle, which bundle_problems() shows. Gradle's resolved library artifacts are not fingerprinted, only the build files that pin them (claim.inputs.dependencies says so), because fingerprinting them would take another Gradle run. Left for the second half of 3b: typed witness values with the target's descriptor, the argument mappings and the class files' identities, a library change.
